solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Charlie, a quiet bully that makes a lot of money

definitions.text: that makes a lot of money
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'something that makes a lot of money'

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written
sh is the call for quiet
to cow someone is to bully or intimidate them

explanation.surface: A noisy playground thug turns out to be quietly running a profitable racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully' reads as a noun but works as the verb to cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash cow is a business or product that reliably generates large profits for its owner.

clue.text: One getting in a flap about time

blocks.note: ca. is circa, Latin for about
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone panics about running out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a flap' sounds like being flustered, but the flap is a cat flap, the little door a pet uses to get in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat is the animal that comes in through a cat flap, so a playful description of the pet.

clue.text: Rascal's stolen goods, including phone, close to telly

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter of the next word is used
to include something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: swag is slang for loot
to phone is to call
the last letter of telly

explanation.surface: A rogue's loot includes a phone, stashed near the television.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a mischievous rascal or scamp, the two words being synonyms.

clue.text: Retro show inspired by revolutionary appeal of The Mousetrap

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the word is read from end to start
something inspired is breathed in, so it goes inside the other word

blocks.note: to show someone out is to see them out
Che Guevara, the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A nostalgic stage production inspired by a radical takes on Agatha Christie's long-running play The Mousetrap.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed show word sits between the H and E of the revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese is the traditional bait a mousetrap uses to lure its victim, so its attraction or appeal.

clue.text: Painting of owl curator and colleague finally revived

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter only of the word before it
something revived is brought back in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
joins the pieces
the last letter of colleague

explanation.surface: A museum's owl expert and a co-worker restore a painting of the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A watercolour is a painting made with pigments dissolved in water.

clue.text: Buried aluminium and half of gold in part of Mexico

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is two of its letters, here the front pair

blocks.note: buried means hidden away
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium
joins the pieces
the first half of gold

explanation.surface: Metal and gold lie buried somewhere in Mexico, like a treasure hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidalgo is also a Spanish nobleman, but here it is the Mexican state.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidalgo is one of the thirty-one states of Mexico, north of Mexico City.

clue.text: Some bloke adopting posh tone

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece is taken inside the other

blocks.note: a bloke is referred to as he
U means upper-class, as opposed to non-U

explanation.surface: A man affects an upper-class accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tone' looks like a voice to match 'posh', but it is a shade of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue is a tone or shade of colour.

clue.text: Doctor that produces bill before treatment of flu? That's terrible

indicators.note: treating something works on it and changes it, so these letters are reorganised

blocks.note: Dr Dre is the rapper and record producer
a bill is a poster, an advertisement
places the bill ahead of what follows
the letters of flu, rearranged

explanation.surface: A GP billing a patient before treating their influenza is behaving terribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' seems medical, but the doctor who produces is Dr Dre, the hip-hop producer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadful is a straightforward synonym of terrible: very bad or unpleasant.

clue.text: Papa John's introducing topping of yellow bananas

indicators.note: in a down entry the topping is the top letter, so the first letter of the word

blocks.note: the john is slang for the toilet
Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the first letter of yellow

explanation.surface: The pizza chain Papa John's launches a pizza topped with bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: Papa John's looks like the pizza chain; read P plus John's LOO, which then introduces the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas is slang for crazy, and loopy is another informal word for mad.

clue.text: Act effecting change

blocks.note: surface reading: a law or deed that brings about reform
setter's reading: change is the money handed back when you have paid too much

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like reforming legislation; the change is coins returned at a till.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying more than is owed is the act that makes the cashier hand back change.

clue.text: Flirt with banker on the phone

indicators.note: what is said on the phone is only heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: a banker is a river, here the Tees in north-east England

explanation.surface: Someone chats up a financier over the telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: A banker is crossword shorthand for a river, something with banks.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease someone can mean to flirt with them, teasing them playfully.

clue.text: Card-carrying official starts to outcast rebels and extremists thus

indicators.note: the start of each following word is its first letter, so only initials are kept

blocks.note: the referee, who carries yellow and red cards
the first letters of outcast, rebels and extremists

explanation.surface: A party member in good standing leads the expulsion of rebels and extremists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card-carrying' suggests party membership, but it is the football referee, the definite article included.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore and thus are synonyms, both meaning consequently or for that reason.

clue.text: Drawn, sick American getting tarted up

indicators.note: something tarted up has been dressed up and altered, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: sick means ill
US is short for American
the letters of tarted, rearranged

explanation.surface: A pale, unwell American is being dressed up flashily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' looks like haggard, matching sick, but it means pictured.
explanation.definitionFit: An illustrated book has been drawn, provided with pictures and sketches.

clue.text: Clever little engine almost crashes

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped
a crash smashes things up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
engine without its final letter

explanation.surface: A smart little engine nearly comes to grief, like a children's story locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligent is a direct synonym of clever: quick to understand and learn.

clue.text: Direct coach one's taken with mum and dad cycling behind

indicators.note: one is the letter I, and taking it away removes that letter from the word
letters cycling go round, so the last moves to the front

blocks.note: a coach is a train carriage; the I goes
mum and dad are parents, cycled one place
places the parents after the coach

explanation.surface: Instructions for a coach trip, with parents riding bikes at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the S of the parents to the front gives the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparent can mean direct and open, with nothing hidden, like a frank manner.

clue.text: My apple contains a bit of bark

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A worried owner sees a nibble of tree bark in their apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bark' suggests a tree, but it is a dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A yap is a short, sharp yelp, a small burst of a dog's barking.

clue.text: Winton?

blocks.note: read as W IN TON: the outer word, a hundred
read as W IN TON: the letter W goes inside

explanation.surface: Just a place name, posed as a question.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the name reads as the instruction W IN TON, and the result describes what Winton is; Wintons exist in Dorset, Cumbria and Queensland.
explanation.definitionFit: Winton is an example of a settlement of that size, so the question mark flags a definition by example.

clue.text: What can I say? Your unfinished baclava is abysmal

indicators.note: unfinished means its end is missing, so the last letter of the dessert goes
something abysmal is a total mess, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the pastry minus its final letter

explanation.surface: A dinner guest, lost for words, admits their half-eaten baklava is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What can I say?' reads as an embarrassed shrug, but asks literally for the stock of words one can use.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's vocabulary is the full range of words available to them, everything they can say.

clue.text: Fun arising when a docked mongrel is impregnated

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the last letter is removed
impregnating fills something, so another piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a mutt is a mongrel, here docked
what does the impregnating, implied by the word

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture: amusement at a short-tailed mongrel getting pregnant.
explanation.walkthrough: The filling is not printed: 'impregnated' both signals the insertion and implies what is inserted, a risqué touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement and fun are synonyms for enjoyment or entertainment.

clue.text: German sacrificing time and opportunity to make instrument

indicators.note: to sacrifice something is to give it up, so that letter goes

blocks.note: Otto, a typical German name, losing one T
T, the letter given up
scope means room or opportunity

explanation.surface: A German gives up his time and a chance in order to build a device.
explanation.definitionFit: An otoscope is a medical instrument doctors use for looking into the ear.

clue.text: Building with high beams

blocks.note: surface reading: a structure with lofty roof timbers
setter's reading: beams of light shining from a tall tower

explanation.walkthrough: Beams suggests rafters; think instead of shafts of light sent out over the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal tower that sends out a high, rotating light to warn and guide ships.

clue.text: Notes made by retired English head

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Memos written by a retired English headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired English head' looks like a former headmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune is a melody, a sequence of musical notes.

clue.text: Condition of mat has deteriorated

indicators.note: something deteriorated has fallen apart, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The state of a doormat has got worse.
explanation.walkthrough: A dusty mat could trigger the very condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a medical condition of the airways causing wheezing and breathlessness.

clue.text: Colour of dead-headed flower

indicators.note: deadheading a plant removes its top, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: the pink, a garden flower, minus its first letter

explanation.surface: The hue of a flower whose spent bloom has been snipped off.
explanation.walkthrough: Colour is a verb: to ink means to colour in. The pink is a dianthus, a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: To ink a drawing is to colour it in, a sense recorded in Chambers.

clue.text: Part of Greek, apparently

indicators.note: a part of the following words holds the answer inside them

blocks.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: Something is apparently a bit Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' does double duty: the answer is part of the Greek alphabet and sits inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Kappa is the tenth letter of the Greek alphabet, so a part of Greek writing.

clue.text: Ambassador stopping pederasts getting thrown in cells

indicators.note: something stopping a gap plugs it, so it sits inside the other letters
things thrown about land in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of pederasts, rearranged
HE, His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A diplomat prevents sex offenders being thrown into prison cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cells' suggests prison, but it means the boxes of a grid of data.
explanation.definitionFit: A spreadsheet is a program laid out as a grid of cells holding figures and formulas.

clue.text: Old, exhausted pitbull with very large setter's dangerous

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word stay

blocks.note: ex means former
pitbull emptied of its middle
OS is outsize, a clothing size
the setter is I, and setter's is I have, I've

explanation.surface: A tired old pit bull combined with a huge setter makes a dangerous pair of dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the dog breed, matching pitbull, but it is the crossword's setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Explosive can mean dangerous, likely to blow up, literally or of a tense situation.

clue.text: She sounds like a drip

indicators.note: sounds like says the answer is heard as the next word

blocks.note: an IV is an intravenous drip

explanation.surface: A dull woman described as sounding like a drip.
explanation.walkthrough: Drip seems to mean a wet person, but a hospital drip is an IV; Ivy is also a creeping, drippy plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a woman's name, so a 'she'.

clue.text: Animal with laugh full of hunger

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: ha is a laugh
a yen is a craving

explanation.surface: A beast with a ravenous laugh, a picture of the laughing hyena.
explanation.walkthrough: The laughing hyena is a scavenger, so the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is an African carnivore known for its laughing call.

clue.text: Belt out the opening of musical number

indicators.note: belt out here means knock out, so the first letter is removed

blocks.note: the musical Hair, losing its first letter

explanation.surface: Sing loudly the overture of a show tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt out' wants to mean sing loudly, but it knocks out a letter. Hair is the 1960s rock musical.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or song, a musical number.

clue.text: 'Smart one overcome by anger' — Othello?

indicators.note: overcome means beaten and replaced, so one letter makes way for a word

blocks.note: smart means neat
one is the Roman numeral I
rage is anger

explanation.surface: A quoted remark about Othello: a smart man undone by his anger.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in the smart word is replaced by the anger word.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's tragedy; the question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: I perform Browning, and I generate cheers

blocks.note: first meaning: a kitchen appliance that browns bread
second meaning: someone proposing a toast, prompting cries of cheers

explanation.walkthrough: Browning looks like the poet, as if reciting his verse, but it is browning toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A toaster is the machine that browns bread, and also a person who proposes a toast with glasses raised.
